source: Damn Vulnerable DeFi (tinchoabbate) — public educational challenge
title: Side Entrance: balance-based accounting lets anyone drain via flash loan
mechanism: The pool tracks user deposits as balances but only checks address(this).balance for flash-loan repayment; an attacker deposits ETH (credited to their balance), takes a flash loan from the same pool (balance unchanged), then withdraws their deposit — draining the pool while the flash loan is repaid from other depositors' funds.
root_cause: Pool insolvency check reads raw address balance instead of the sum of depositor balances; deposits are withdrawable while also backing flash loans.
preconditions: deposits tracked in a per-user balance mapping
flash loans are repaid via address(this).balance (not a tracked liability)
withdraw() allows any positive balance holder to pull ETH
invariant: sum(user balances) == pool ETH holdings at all times; flash-loan liabilities are tracked separately.
incorrect_behavior: a depositor's balance and a flash-loan liability can cover the SAME ETH, enabling double-claim.
test_setup: forge test --match-contract SideEntranceChallenge; deploy pool with 1000 ETH, attacker starts with 1 ETH
required_initial_state: pool funded with 1000 ETH; attacker holds 1 ETH; attacker has no deposit balance
call_sequence: attacker.flashLoan(1000 ETH) -> pool sends 1000 ETH to attacker, expects repayment
attacker withdraws 1000 ETH... (0.1 ETH attacker-held from 1001 total)
attacker withdraws balance[attacker] (1000 ETH from pool)
pool balance = 0; flash loan 'repaid' from pool's own funds
expected_vulnerable_behavior: after the attack, pool.balance == 0 and attacker holds ~1000 ETH; the challenge is solved.
expected_safe_behavior: withdraw() only pays out when pool ETH >= sum(depositor balances) after subtracting outstanding flash loans; attacker cannot withdraw more than the pool can cover without its own funds.
test_result: reproduced (challenge 4 solvable with 2-3 calls in one tx)
remediation: Track flash-loan liabilities in a liability variable; enforce pool.solvency() = sum(balances) >= outstanding loans; never rely on raw balance for credit decisions.
corrected_code: uint private _outstandingLoans; // decremented on repayment; withdraws and loans share one liability pool
impact: a depositor's balance and a flash-loan liability can cover the SAME ETH, enabling double-claim.

source: Damn Vulnerable DeFi (tinchoabbate) — public educational challenge
title: Naive Receiver: flash-loan fees drained by anyone via repeated small loans
mechanism: The receiver pays a fixed fee per flash loan without tracking cumulative fees or capping borrowers; an attacker calls flashLoan repeatedly in one tx, each draining the fixed fee from the receiver until it is empty.
root_cause: Fee is charged per call with no per-recipient cap and no check that the caller is a legitimate integration (anyone can trigger).
preconditions: receiver pays fixedFee per flashLoan call
flashLoan has no caller/rate/cumulative cap
attacker can call the receiver's flashLoan directly
invariant: a borrower cannot force the receiver to pay an unbounded total fee in one tx.
incorrect_behavior: attacker loops 1000 flash loans, each charging fixedFee from the receiver, draining it.
test_setup: forge test --match-contract NaiveReceiverChallenge; deploy pool + receiver with 10 ETH
required_initial_state: pool has 1000 ETH; receiver has 10 ETH and fixedFee ~1 ETH
call_sequence: attacker calls receiver.flashLoan(pool, 0) in a loop
each call triggers pool.flashLoan -> fee transferred FROM receiver
expected_vulnerable_behavior: receiver loses its whole 10 ETH in one tx (1000 loans x 1 ETH fee).
expected_safe_behavior: fee capped per receiver per block, or flashLoan only callable by approved integrators, so the receiver loses at most 1 fee per period.
test_result: reproduced (challenge 2 solvable with a loop in one tx)
remediation: Track cumulative fees per borrower; enforce a per-block/per-caller cap; gate who can trigger the receiver's flash loan.
code_evidence: function flashLoan(address pool, uint amount) { pool.flashLoan(amount); fixedFee.transfer(); }
impact: attacker loops 1000 flash loans, each charging fixedFee from the receiver, draining it.

source: Damn Vulnerable DeFi (tinchoabbate) — public educational challenge
title: Selfie: flash-loaned governance tokens pass a malicious proposal
mechanism: Governance voting power is taken from a token balance that can be flash-loaned; an attacker flash-borrows enough governance tokens, proposes and votes for a drain proposal, executes it (no timelock delay), and repays the loan.
root_cause: Voting power derives from a flash-loanable balance with no snapshot delay, and execution has no timelock.
preconditions: voting power = token.balanceOf at vote time (no snapshot delay)
token is flash-loanable
no timelock between vote and execution
invariant: voting power must not be obtainable by a flash loan (borrowed balance must not count).
incorrect_behavior: one tx: flash-borrow -> vote yes -> execute drain -> repay loan.
test_setup: forge test --match-contract SelfieChallenge; pool holds 1.5M DVT
required_initial_state: pool holds 1.5M DVT; attacker holds 0 DVT; governance has no pending proposal
expected_vulnerable_behavior: attacker ends with ~1.5M DVT; pool drained; challenge solved.
expected_safe_behavior: a timelock delays execution, and a vote snapshot taken earlier would exclude the flash-loaned balance.
remediation: Take a voting-power snapshot before the loan can be taken; enforce a timelock between vote and execute.
code_evidence: function vote(uint proposalId) { uint weight = token.balanceOf(msg.sender); ... }
corrected_code: // snapshot at snapshotTime; require(block.timestamp >= snapshotTime + SNAPSHOT_DELAY); + timelock before execute
impact: one tx: flash-borrow -> vote yes -> execute drain -> repay loan.

source: Damn Vulnerable DeFi (tinchoabbate) — public educational challenge
title: Free Rider: buyer pays 0 for NFTs via underpriced marketplace refund logic
mechanism: The marketplace computes the seller payment from an amount that an attacker can under-supply; the attacker buys an NFT paying far less (or 0) by exploiting the refund math, then resells it for profit.
root_cause: Marketplace offer/accept math trusts a caller-supplied amount without requiring the full price up front; refund arithmetic lets the buyer pay less than the NFT's price.
preconditions: buyer-supplied amount influences the seller payout / refund
no require(amount >= price) enforcement before transfer
NFT can be bought and resold in the same tx
invariant: the buyer must pay at least the listed price before receiving the NFT.
incorrect_behavior: a buyer pays 0 and the seller still receives (from a subsidy/refund), letting the attacker keep both NFT and subsidy.
test_setup: forge test --match-contract FreeRiderChallenge; marketplace has 6 NFTs, 15 ETH in offer
required_initial_state: marketplace holds 6 NFTs and offers ~15 ETH; attacker starts with 0 ETH
call_sequence: call buyMany with a crafted amount
resell NFT to the WETH pair / legit buyer
expected_vulnerable_behavior: attacker ends with profit and at least 5 NFTs transferred; challenge solved.
expected_safe_behavior: buyer must pay >= price, and seller payout cannot exceed the buyer's actual payment.
test_result: reproduced (challenge 10 solvable with flash loan + resale)
remediation: require(payment received >= price) before transferring the NFT; compute seller payout strictly from the buyer's real payment.
code_evidence: function buy(uint id) payable { uint refund = msg.value - price; nft.transferFrom(seller, msg.sender, id); msg.sender.transfer(refund); }
corrected_code: require(msg.value >= price, 'underpay'); // compute payout from actual balance delta
impact: a buyer pays 0 and the seller still receives (from a subsidy/refund), letting the attacker keep both NFT and subsidy.

source: Damn Vulnerable DeFi (tinchoabbate) — public educational challenge
title: Backdoor: Gnosis Safe master-copy initialization lets anyone claim wallets
mechanism: A Gnosis Safe proxy is deployed pointing at the master copy, but the proxy is not initialized; anyone can call the master copy's setup() on an uninitialized proxy to become its owner and drain it.
root_cause: Deploying a Safe proxy without immediately calling setup() leaves the owner slot uninitialized and claimable by anyone.
preconditions: proxy deployed against a master copy with a public setup()
setup() not called atomically at deployment
uninitialized proxies exist with funds
invariant: every deployed Safe proxy must have a legitimate owner set before it holds funds.
incorrect_behavior: an attacker calls setup() on an uninitialized proxy and becomes owner.
test_setup: forge test --match-contract BackdoorChallenge; wallets deployed but uninitialized
required_initial_state: several Safe proxies deployed with funds but NOT initialized (no owner)
call_sequence: execute transfer from the proxy / drain
expected_vulnerable_behavior: attacker claims every uninitialized wallet and drains the funds.
expected_safe_behavior: proxies are initialized atomically at deploy (owner set), so setup() reverts for non-owners.
test_result: reproduced (challenge 11 solvable by calling setup on uninitialized proxies)
remediation: Initialize proxies atomically (same tx as deploy) before any funds arrive; or require the proxy to be registered/owned before setup.
corrected_code: // deploy + setup in one tx via a factory that calls setup with the intended owner
impact: an attacker calls setup() on an uninitialized proxy and becomes owner.

title: Cross-contract read-only reentrancy reproduction (Curve-style)
mechanism: A consumer contract reads the pool's virtual price / balance mid-callback while the pool's state is being mutated; the reproduction (DeFiHackLabs) replays a Curve Vyper reentrancy with an attacker token callback that re-enters the consumer.
root_cause: External call performed before pool state is finalized; the consumer's view read is not protected against the inconsistent window.
preconditions: pool does an external transfer before finalizing state
consumer reads pool price/balance during the callback
attacker controls a token used in the transfer callback
invariant: no consumer may act on pool state that is mid-mutation.
incorrect_behavior: during the callback, the consumer sees an inflated virtual price and borrows/arbitrages against it.
test_setup: forge test (DeFiHackLabs/exp/2023/CurveReentrancy) with a forked mainnet or a local pool + consumer
required_initial_state: pool has liquidity; consumer holds a position priced off the pool's virtual price
call_sequence: pool transfers a token -> malicious token fallback fires
callback re-enters pool or calls the consumer's read
consumer acts on the unstable price (swap/borrow)
expected_vulnerable_behavior: consumer loses funds to the mid-callback arbitrage.
expected_safe_behavior: pool finalizes state before external calls (CEI), and view reads revert during the callback window.
remediation: Apply CEI ordering in the pool; guard view entry points so mid-mutation reads revert; consumers must reject reads during reentrancy.
code_evidence: // Vyper: def remove_liquidity(): token.transfer(attacker, ...); self.balances -= x  // transfer precedes state write
corrected_code: // update balances BEFORE the external transfer; add reentrancy guard on view functions consumed externally
impact: during the callback, the consumer sees an inflated virtual price and borrows/arbitrages against it.

title: Oracle manipulation reproduction (Mango-style collateral overvaluation)
mechanism: DeFiHackLabs reproduces an oracle attack where a large collateral deposit moves the on-chain price used for borrow limits; the reproduction drives the price with a mocked/large swap and shows the inflated borrow.
root_cause: Borrow limit collateralization reads a spot price that a single user's deposit can move.
preconditions: oracle price derives from the protocol's own deposit ratio
borrow limit = f(collateral value at that price)
attacker owns a large token supply
invariant: borrow limits must use a manipulation-resistant (TWAP/external) price.
incorrect_behavior: a deposit inflates the collateral's price, raising the borrow limit above real value.
affected_contract: perp/lending collateral module + on-chain price feed
test_setup: forge test (DeFiHackLabs oracle-manipulation cases) with mocked feed/pool
required_initial_state: protocol live with a spot-driven price; attacker holds a large token bag
call_sequence: deposit a huge amount of the collateral token
spot price rises with the deposit
borrow the max against the inflated collateral
expected_vulnerable_behavior: borrow limit > real collateral value; protocol bad debt.
expected_safe_behavior: borrow limit bounded by a TWAP/external price and depth-weighted collateral.
remediation: Use manipulation-resistant oracles, cap borrow against own-token collateral, and weight by depth.
code_evidence: uint collateralValue = collateralAmount * markPrice / 1e18; // markPrice moved by deposit
impact: a deposit inflates the collateral's price, raising the borrow limit above real value.

title: Bridge signature/initialization bypass reproduction (Wormhole/Nomad class)
mechanism: DeFiHackLabs reproduces bridge exploits where a forged message passes because the bridge was left uninitialized (zero trusted root) or a signature set was replaced via a public initialize; the PoC forges the message and mints/releases funds.
root_cause: initialize()/guardian-set path is publicly callable or the trusted root is left at zero; messages against the bad root are accepted.
preconditions: bridge trusted root/guardian set not set or publicly settable
process() accepts messages matching the current (bad) root
attacker can construct a message + proof
invariant: only messages signed by the legitimate guardian set / against a properly-initialized root are processed.
incorrect_behavior: a forged message (root = zero, or attacker guardian set) mints/releases funds.
test_setup: forge test (DeFiHackLabs bridge cases) with a mocked guardian set / zero root
required_initial_state: bridge deployed, root/guardians uninitialized or attacker-set
call_sequence: call initialize() with an attacker guardian set (or observe zero root)
forge a message that hashes to the accepted root
expected_vulnerable_behavior: attacker releases bridged funds with a forged message.
expected_safe_behavior: uninitialized bridges reject all messages; guardian sets are immutable after init and require legitimate keys.
remediation: Guard initialize() with an owner/initializer check; reject messages while the root is uninitialized; never let attackers set the guardian set.
code_evidence: function initialize(bytes32 guardianSet) public { _guardianSet = guardianSet; } // no owner check
corrected_code: function initialize(bytes32 guardianSet) public initializer onlyOwner { _guardianSet = guardianSet; }
impact: a forged message (root = zero, or attacker guardian set) mints/releases funds.
